situation: A check-out makes the room dirty
given: a clean room with a Guest in house at a Property where housekeeping is available
when: the Guest is checked out and the worker delivers stay.checked_out
then: the room is dirty, stamped with the time of the delivery and no Staff Member

given: a Guest in a bed under a room
then: the room is dirty, not the bed: the room holds the status (ADR 0029)

given: a Property whose Units are beds with no parent (ADR 0004)
when: a Guest in one is checked out
then: that bed is dirty: with no room above it, it holds its own status

given: a check-out already marked the room dirty
when: the same event is delivered again
then: nothing changes: the delivery row refuses a second run by the dispatcher (proved by tests/integration/outbox.test.ts), and a run that gets past it — the delivery row lost — finds its own mark stamped after the departure and writes nothing

situation: Cleaned before the worker got there
given: a check-out at 10:00 and the desk marking the room clean at 10:00:01
when: the worker delivers the event after that
then: the room stays clean: a status changed after the departure is the later word and is kept

given: a room marked inspected at 09:00
then: the room is dirty: the mark was made before the Guest left and is overwritten

given: a caller with no worker context
then: refused with 42501, before anything is read

given: a worker context for Organization A
when: it names an event belonging to Organization B
then: refused with 42501

given: a Property whose housekeeping capability is off or whose Subscription has lapsed
then: no status is written, so no front desk that never bought housekeeping sees a room turn dirty

given: an event that is not stay.checked_out, or whose Stay is not departed
when: the function is called with it
then: it marks nothing and returns false

given: ranza_worker
when: it tries to read or write housekeeping_unit_status directly
then: refused: it holds no grant on the table and reaches it only through the one function (ADR 0027)

situation: A status on a bed under a room
given: a bed with a parent
when: any role writes a housekeeping row for it
then: refused with 55000: its room answers for it

given: a Property with rooms, some with rows and some without
when: a Staff Member reaching it opens Housekeeping
then: every room and parentless bed comes back once with its status; one with no row reads clean; a room let by the bed shows how many beds it has

given: a Staff Member not assigned to a Property
then: nothing comes back, indistinguishable from a Property with no rooms

given: housekeeping disabled at the Property or the Subscription lapsed
then: nothing comes back: the read carries the commercial gates in its own statement

given: a Property with no Units
then: it says there are no rooms and points to Rooms, rather than showing an empty table

given: tr, en and ar
when: the board is opened in each
then: every string is translated, Arabic mirrors, and status reads as a word with an icon, never colour alone

given: a dirty room that is then blocked, then unblocked
when: the board is read at each step
then: it is dirty throughout: blocking is accommodation_units.status and does not touch this one

given: any write to a housekeeping row
then: status_changed_at is now and status_changed_by is the acting Staff Member or null for the worker, stamped by the database rather than stated by the caller

given: a Property whose rooms went dirty, and which then stops using housekeeping
then: every room reads ready again and the stored statuses are untouched: nothing there can clear a status any more, so none may hold a check-in up

given: a dirty room and a Staff Member holding housekeeping.update_status
then: it is clean, and the audit record names them, the room and the status it had

given: three dirty rooms
when: they are selected and marked inspected together
then: all three are inspected in one transaction, each with its own audit record

given: a selection naming two beds of the same room
then: the room is marked once; the statement names each room one time so Postgres does not refuse it for touching a row twice

given: a Staff Member whose role lacks housekeeping.update_status
when: they try to mark a room
then: refused by the policy with 42501, surfaced as a refusal

given: a room marked clean that was not
then: it is dirty, audited, and no reason is asked for

given: a clean room
when: it is marked clean again, or the form is submitted twice
then: it stays clean and nothing fails; each submission is audited

given: a Staff Member of Organization A
when: they name a room of Organization B
then: refused: the row is invisible and the write names nothing

given: the capability off or the Subscription lapsed
when: a Staff Member with the permission marks a room
then: refused by the policy: all five gates bound the write

given: a Staff Member
when: they name status_changed_by or status_changed_at in a write
then: refused with 42501: those columns are in no grant

given: a request naming no Units, more than sixty, or a status outside dirty, clean and inspected
then: refused before any statement runs

given: a new Organization
then: owner, manager, front desk and housekeeping hold housekeeping.update_status; finance does not

given: a Staff Member who reaches the Property without the permission
then: they see every status and no control that changes one

given: a mark refused by the database, which happens because the viewer's permission, the capability or the Subscription has changed
then: a translated message, nothing claimed as done, and the board the server now sends: read-only when the permission went, so no selection control is shown (decided by the product owner, 2026-09-24; it once said the selection was kept, which no real refusal can show)

given: an arriving Reservation on a dirty room
then: nothing is written; the desk is told the room is not ready and offered to check in anyway

given: the same warning
then: the Guest is checked in, the audit record notes the room was not ready, and the room stays dirty

given: an arriving Reservation on a clean room
then: it checks in with no warning

situation: Cleaned between the warning and the confirmation
given: a warning shown, then the room marked clean
then: the check-in succeeds and the audit record does not claim the room was not ready: readiness is read again in the check-in's own statement

given: arrivals whose rooms are dirty, clean and inspected
then: each row says whether its room is ready, as a word and an icon

given: an Organization with inspection on and a clean room
then: not ready until inspected

given: the Organization default on and a Property set off
when: readiness is read at that Property
then: a clean room is ready there

given: a Property row with no value of its own
then: the Organization default applies, and with no default at all inspection is off

given: an Organization with a default
when: a second default row is inserted
then: refused by a partial unique index; a total one would not have constrained it because null is not equal to null

given: a Staff Member with reach to one Property
then: refused: the default needs Organization-wide reach; they may override their own Property

given: clean and inspected rooms
when: inspection is switched on or off
then: no stored status changes; only what counts as ready does

given: a Staff Member without accommodation.configure
then: refused by the policy

given: any change to the default or an override, including a reset
then: an audit record names who changed it, where, from what and to what

given: a Property following the default
when: the inspection card on the Housekeeping screen is read
then: it shows Use Organization default with the inherited value beside it, and a preview of the flow that follows

given: a Property with its own value
then: its override is cleared rather than deleted, and it follows the default again

situation: A room never marked, under inspection
given: inspection switched on and a room that has no status row
then: it is clean, as the board shows it, and so it waits for an inspection like a room marked clean; switching inspection on means every room waits until it is inspected

situation: Daily cleaning of a room still in use
given: a Guest staying several nights
then: proposed answer: built as slice 4 (HK-S4-01 .. HK-S4-21). An occupied room due for a clean is a read over the schedule, never a status: it is not dirty, not unready and never blocks a check-in. Still deferred inside it: cleaning that differs per room or per person, and a Today figure for rooms due

situation: A bed's own status in a shared room
given: a room let by the bed
then: deferred: in a room let by the bed a departure still dirties the whole room and every bed waits. Not built with stayover cleaning because it relaxes the holder trigger and changes app.unit_status_holder, app.housekeeping_states, app.unit_is_ready and app.mark_unit_dirty_after_check_out, which the board, the arrivals list, check-in and the room calendar all read; that is a change to hotel turnover and needs its own design and its own sabotage of every reader. Stayover cleaning does not depend on it, because a stayover is the room's and never a bed's

given: a check-out marked by the worker
then: deferred: the worker has no audit identity (audit.records.actor_id is a Staff Member); the departure itself is audited as stay.checked_out and the row's null status_changed_by says the check-out did it

given: a room marked clean
when: a manager asks which housekeeper did it
then: out of scope: the audit names who pressed the button; assigning work to a named housekeeper is a later feature

given: any housekeeping change
then: out of scope: nothing here is charged or refunded

given: a room that needs fixing
when: it is taken out of service
then: out of scope: maintenance (RANZ-33) owns it on accommodation_units.status

situation: Checked in before the worker got there
given: a Guest was checked out of a room and the worker has not yet delivered the departure, or is down
when: the next Guest is checked in to that room
then: the desk is asked, as for a dirty room: a room is not ready while a Guest has left it since its status last changed; a mark made after the departure is what it says, and the worker leaves it alone

situation: The board before the worker gets there
given: a Guest was checked out of a room and the worker has not yet written the room dirty, or is down
when: the board is read or the room is marked
then: the room reads dirty since the departure, is counted and filtered as dirty, and a mark records dirty as what it replaced: the board says what readiness says, whatever the stored row still reads

given: a room was marked after its Guest left
when: the departed Stay is written again, re-dated or merely touched, by any role
then: the moment the Guest left does not move, so the room keeps what the later mark said: the database stamps it once as the Stay departs, carries it over on every update, and grants the runtime role no write to it

situation: A screen opened at a Property where housekeeping is off
given: ?property= names a Property where housekeeping is switched off, or one the viewer does not reach. Every link inside the workspace names one: with none in the URL, the Property the switcher names
then: the empty state, never the rooms of another Property; the switcher names that Property when the viewer reaches it and no Property when not. Today, which shows a Property's day rather than an empty state, goes back to Today with no ?property= instead. A URL typed by hand with no ?property= at all still opens on the first Property that has housekeeping, and the switcher then names the first Property with Today, which can be a different one (kept by the owner, 2026-09-24; found by the RANZ-28 evidence run)

situation: A check-out dirties the room through the worker
given: a Guest checked in and out through the screens with inspection on and the worker not yet round
when: the worker's dispatcher runs and a cleaner then opens Housekeeping
then: before it runs the stored status is still what the room was given and the board already reads the room dirty (HK-S1-22); after it the delivery is recorded and the stored status is dirty with no Staff Member behind it; the cleaner finds the room dirty, marks it clean and it waits for inspection, then marks it inspected and it is ready, each stamped with who pressed the button
test_name: housekeeping.spec.ts: a check-out leaves the room dirty through the worker, and a cleaner takes it to inspected

situation: Ready to let counts a room a Guest can be put in
given: a Property with an inspected room nobody is in, a clean room a Guest is in, and a room out of service
when: the board's Ready to let figure is read
then: it counts the inspected room alone, by the definition Today and the board's own ?show=ready filter use: a room somebody is in, or out of service, is housekeeping-ready and is not counted (RANZ-57, RANZ-52)
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: counts as ready to let only a ready room nobody is in (HK-06, RANZ-57); housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: Ready to let does not count a room somebody is in, and the board opens on what to clean first

situation: The board opens on what to clean first
given: a dirty room a Guest arrives into today, a clean room with no movement, and a room a Guest leaves today
when: the board is opened with no sort chosen
then: the rooms come in the order Today's clean-first list uses (arrival, inspect for arrival, leaving, queued), then ready rooms with an arrival or a departure, then the rest in building, floor and name order; each room with a movement says so in a Today column (Arrival today, Arrival · inspect, Leaving today); choosing a sort replaces the order
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: says what the day asks of a room beside its status (HK-04); housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: Ready to let does not count a room somebody is in, and the board opens on what to clean first

given: a Property with rooms on more than one floor, and one with rooms on a single floor or none
then: the first offers a Floor filter listing each floor, and No floor where a room has none, with how many rooms each holds; the second offers none, because there is nothing to narrow by; a floor deep link from Today still opens the narrowed board
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: offers a floor filter only when the Property has more than one floor (HK-05); housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: Ready to let does not count a room somebody is in, and the board opens on what to clean first

situation: A room never marked, and a mark from another year
given: a room with no status row and a room whose last change was in an earlier year
then: the first says Never marked, not Not recorded yet, which read like a failure; the second shows its year beside the day and time, so an old mark does not read as a recent one
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: names a room never marked, and a mark from another year with its year (HK-13)

situation: A confirmation where a phone can see it
given: a phone, and rooms ticked a screen below the line that says what a mark did
then: the result rides at the foot of the window above the dock, clears itself after six seconds when it is good news, and stays until the next mark when it is a refusal; the mark buttons are at least 44 px high on touch, and Mark dirty is set apart from the other two
test_name: housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: a phone says a mark landed where it can be seen, and the stale-link page points at the Property control

situation: A link to a Property where the viewer has no housekeeping, with other Properties to choose
given: a stale or foreign ?property=, and a viewer who has housekeeping at another Property
then: the empty state of HK-S1-24 stands, and adds that the Property control in the bar chooses another Property; for a viewer with housekeeping nowhere it says nothing more, since there is nothing to choose
test_name: housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: a phone says a mark landed where it can be seen, and the stale-link page points at the Property control

situation: Who may not change the setting is told in a sentence
given: a Staff Member who may change neither the Organization default nor this Property's value
then: one sentence says whether a cleaned room waits for inspection at this Property and that a manager can change it, with no disabled control to try; a Staff Member who may change one of the two still sees both, the other disabled with its reason (HK-S3-07)
test_name: inspection-settings.test.tsx: tells a reader without the permission what applies in a sentence, with no control to try (HK-S3-12)

situation: Report a problem from the room's row
given: a Staff Member who may report a maintenance problem, on the Housekeeping board
when: they press Report a problem on a room's row
then: Maintenance opens with its report form already on that room; a Staff Member who may not report is shown no link
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: offers a report-a-problem link on the room's row to somebody who may report (MAINT-10); housekeeping-ux.spec.ts: a phone says a mark landed where it can be seen, and the stale-link page points at the Property control

situation: Select every room the filter holds
given: a filter of more rooms than a page
then: the bar offers Select all N rooms in this filter, one press takes them all and the count says so; the board opens on fifty rooms a page (HK-09)

situation: The bulk bar stays in reach on a phone
given: rooms ticked far down a long list on a phone
then: the bar stays at the top of the screen, and the row's tick, the pagination arrows and the row menu are at least 44 px to a finger (HK-02, HK-08)

situation: A phone says whether anybody is in the room, and the counts once
given: a phone, and a board of rooms
then: under each room's number sit its status, what the day asks of it and whether anybody is in it (Vacant, Guest in house or Out of service), so whether to knock is on the first screen without swiping the table; the Dirty, Clean and Inspected counts are the status chips and not also tiles, so Rooms and Ready to let make one short row and the first room is on the first screen (HOUSEKEEPING-04, HOUSEKEEPING-05)
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: says on a phone whether anybody is in the room, beside its status (HOUSEKEEPING-04)

situation: The bulk bar is short on a phone
given: rooms ticked on a phone
when: the bar over the list is drawn
then: its three marks are icons, each still named for a screen reader and still 44 px, so the bar is two short rows and not three; that the bar still pushes the list down when it appears belongs to the data table and is handed to the shell lane (HOUSEKEEPING-03)
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: keeps the bulk bar to icons on a phone, each button still named (HOUSEKEEPING-03)

situation: Report a problem from the row's menu on a phone
given: a Staff Member who may mark rooms and report a problem, on a phone
when: they look for Report a problem
then: it is an item of the room's menu and no grey line beside the tick, which a thumb aiming at the tick could open instead; from md up the line stays under the room number; a viewer with no menu keeps the line, at a thumb's height (HOUSEKEEPING-06)
test_name: housekeeping-board.test.tsx: reaches Report a problem from the row menu, and leaves the inline link to a desktop (HOUSEKEEPING-06)

situation: One tap marks a room clean, and the confirmation offers Undo
given: a dirty room on a phone, and a housekeeper working down a floor
then: it advances Dirty to Clean (and Clean to Inspected where inspection is on) in the same tap, and the six-second confirmation carries an Undo that marks the room back, audited like any mark (HK-S2-05); the row menu keeps the rarer jumps. Comparable: Mews and Opera Cloud housekeeping task lists. Proposed, not built: a new gesture on the status (HOUSEKEEPING-02)

situation: A room says that a request or a fault is open for it
given: a room with an open guest request or an open maintenance request
then: its row carries a small marker with the count that opens the filtered request page, so a housekeeper learns of a fault without opening two other pages. Comparable: Mews and Cloudbeds housekeeping, which show a room's open tasks on its card. Proposed, not built (HOUSEKEEPING-16)

situation: The board's filters survive leaving it
given: a housekeeper on Dirty and floor 3 who reports a fault
then: Dirty and the floor are in the address, and the way back from Maintenance opened from a room is the board as it was left and not Today. Needs the data table to keep a filter in the address and the page bar to take an origin, both the shell lane's. Proposed, not built (HOUSEKEEPING-07)

situation: Each room is a card on a phone
given: a phone and a board of rooms
then: there is no sideways scroll: room, status, today and occupancy are one card and Last changed sits in the menu. The same proposal as the data table's card layout for every listing. Comparable: Mews and Opera Cloud mobile housekeeping. Proposed, not built (HOUSEKEEPING-04)

situation: A room in use falls due on the schedule
given: a Property cleaning rooms in use every day, every N days or one weekday a week, and rooms somebody arrived in on different days
then: a room is due once its cycle began on a day before the day the schedule next falls on: every day is the day after the cycle began, every N days is N days on, weekly is the next such weekday. The cycle begins at the latest of the day the earliest person still in the room arrived, the last time the room was marked clean or inspected, and the last stayover clean. A room that is overdue stays due until it is cleaned, so a missed day is not lost

situation: A Property sets how often rooms in use are cleaned
given: a Staff Member who may configure the Property's accommodation
when: they choose never, every N days (one is every day) or one weekday a week, and save it, or choose to follow the default again
then: the Property cleans on that schedule from the next read; following the default again clears the value and keeps the row, and the audit record keeps what it was. Nothing the Property holds is rewritten, because whether a room is due is read and never stored

situation: A schedule the table would not store
given: any Staff Member who may configure
when: a save names a weekday that does not exist, an interval beyond fourteen days, a weekly schedule that also names an interval, or an interval with a weekday
then: refused by a check constraint on the table; the form offers only values the constraint accepts, and a function handed one anyway lists no rooms rather than guessing

given: a Staff Member without accommodation.configure, one who does not reach the Property, one of another Organization, or a Property without housekeeping
then: refused by the insert and update policies: accommodation.configure, reach to the Property and the housekeeping capability, the same gates as the inspection setting's Property override. An update changes the cadence and nothing about whose it is

situation: An occupied room due for a clean is not dirty
given: a room somebody is in that is due a stayover clean, and the bed beside it empty
when: the board and check-in read its status
then: the room reads clean, is still ready to let as far as housekeeping goes, and a check-in of the bed beside it is not warned or refused. Stayover writes nothing to housekeeping_unit_status and nothing in turnover reads it, so a hotel's turnover reads exactly as it did. Whether a room is due is computed when read, not marked by a job: it follows from the schedule, the arrival and the last clean, so a changed schedule re-draws the list at once, a missed day is not lost, and no job exists that could stall silently

situation: Rooms that turnover or maintenance own are not listed
given: a room that is dirty, or out of service, with somebody in it
then: neither is listed: a dirty room is turnover's work, and marking it clean starts the cycle over; a room out of service is not cleaned on a schedule

situation: A room everyone in it leaves today
given: a room whose every stay ends today
then: it is not listed: it is about to be turnover. A room with an open-ended stay, or one person staying on, is listed

given: a Staff Member holding housekeeping.update_status with reach to the Property
when: they press Mark cleaned on a room in use
then: a clean is recorded for the day. A role without that permission, somebody of another Organization, and a Property without housekeeping are refused by the insert policy; the front desk and the housekeeping role hold the permission by default

given: a room let by the bed, with people in two beds
when: its stayover is listed or recorded
then: it is one line for the room, counting both people and dating the cycle from the first arrival; a clean recorded against a bed under a room is refused, because a bed is cleaned with its room, as it is for turnover

given: a room already cleaned today
when: Mark cleaned is pressed again, or two people press it together
then: one clean is recorded, the second press says it was already done and writes no audit record, and a partial unique index makes two live cleans of one room on one day impossible

situation: The date and the actor are the database's
given: a Staff Member pressing Mark cleaned
then: cleaned_on is the Property's business date and cleaned_by the acting Staff Member, stamped by a trigger; neither column is in the insert grant, so a caller cannot postpone the next clean by naming a later date or claim another actor

given: a recorded clean
then: no delete policy and no delete grant on either table: a mistaken press is undone, which stamps the row, and a schedule is cleared to the default

given: a room cleaned today by a press that was a mistake
when: a Staff Member holding housekeeping.update_status presses Undo on the card
then: the row is stamped undone with who and when, the room is due again at once, and the room can be cleaned again the same day; a role without the permission cannot take it back. The audit record says it was taken back

situation: Only today's press can be undone
given: a press made on an earlier business day
when: anyone tries to take it back
then: refused by the update policy: a press from last week taken back today would re-open a room that was due then and is not now, and rewrite what the board said on the days between

situation: Stayover due beside turnover, by block and floor
given: a Property cleaning rooms in use, with rooms in more than one block or on more than one floor
then: Stayover due is a tab beside Turnover with its count; the list is grouped by block and floor, filtered by block and by floor with each chip counting its rooms, and each card shows the room, who is in it, whether it is due today or overdue by how many days, when it was last cleaned or since when they have been in, and a Mark cleaned button. Done cards keep their place, so a run of presses never moves the card under the thumb

situation: One press, with undo, on the card
given: a housekeeper holding housekeeping.update_status
then: the card answers at once as Cleaned today with Undo in the place of the button, no dialog and no reason asked: there is nothing the gesture cannot carry. A refusal after the press puts the card back and says so

situation: The operating model picks the default, in the app
given: a Property that has chosen no schedule
then: a hotel starts at every day and a dormitory at one weekday a week; the application resolves it and hands the answer to the module and to the database function, which read no operating model. A hotel that wants weekly or never, and a dormitory that wants daily, set exactly that

situation: A reader who may look and not mark
given: a Staff Member without housekeeping.update_status
then: they see every room and who is due and no Mark cleaned or Undo button, and a line saying why; the policy is the boundary, the hidden button is courtesy

situation: Every press and every change is audited
given: a press, an undo or a change of schedule
then: housekeeping.stayover_cleaned and housekeeping.stayover_undone are written per room with its name, and housekeeping.stayover_set with the schedule before and after, in the same transaction as the write, and read in the audit log in the reader's language

situation: Nothing due, everything done, and never
given: a Property whose rooms are all cleaned, or with nobody in a room, or whose schedule is never
then: with nothing due the tab says so and names the schedule; with everything cleaned for today the list says so above the cards that can still be undone; with a schedule of never there is no Stayover tab at all and the board is exactly as it was

given: a Staff Member reading in any of the three
when: they use Stayover due and its setting
then: every string, weekday and plural is in the typed catalogue in the three languages, Arabic mirrors with logical directions, and the audit log words the three actions

situation: A dormitory does not say housekeeping
given: a Property run as a student dormitory, read by its staff in any of the three languages
when: they look at the rail, the page bar, the Rooms and Configuration links to the screen, and the schedule setting
then: the screen is called Cleaning (Temizlik, التنظيف) in the dormitory words, and a hotel Property still says Housekeeping; the code, the permission and the capability keep their names (ADR 0057: words only)

given: a Property with a stayover schedule, read on a phone
when: the Housekeeping board opens on Turnover
then: there is no tab bar above the turnover list: the way to the stayover list is a third tile in the counts row that says how many are due and opens them, so the first room is no further down than it was; the stayover list carries the tab bar for the way back
